notes: Much of the guide copy predates the installed build. The copy and most of the evidence were checked on 0.1.78-3795b4c (7 October 2026). The docs now install 0.1.78-c1fa197, which carries Biscuit's #206 Nudge changes, and the evidence's c1fa197 note says the copy was not re-checked against #206. The installed types and source contradict the guide in five places. (1) showClose defaults to true, so the close button shows by default on stacked-prominent and inline-compact. The guide says "Add a close button when people may dismiss it", and its Sources note says "the package adds it only when asked". (2) title and body default to empty, and the default button renders only when buttonLabel or onPressButton is set. The guide says "Nudge’s own copy is a placeholder", and its Don't caption says "Without props it reads “Split payment” and “Button”". (3) buttonSlot={null} now removes the button; the 3795b4c evidence says it still rendered. (4) The root is a region named by its title (c1fa197 evidence), while the Sources note says "The card has no role or name on the web". (5) Nudge now has testID. A further point comes from reading the installed Nudge source, not the types or the evidence, and it has not been checked in the browser: Nudge sets Context Nudge&Alert itself unless the caller or the theme already set a Context. That would make the Don't caption "The button grows to 42 px and outweighs the message" true only when a surrounding Context is set. So the guidance keeps the guide's intent but leans on package facts where they differ. The close button is shown when people may dismiss the nudge; the fact-based rule says to set showClose false otherwise. The Don't pairs about copy and context use the Do caption as their why, not the stale Don't caption. No evidence fact or gap is recorded for behaviour that #206 changed. The content sentence "so always set all three" is marked ambiguous: its stated reason (placeholder copy) is stale, and compact never renders a title while detailed ignores the body and button. The examples pass the Nudge's mode object to the ListItem children, although the evidence says slot children already get the Nudge's modes. The guide names no other component to use instead, so avoidWhen is empty.

examples.purpose: A split-payment suggestion on a payment screen, in a lavender appearance; the screen handles the button and removes the nudge on close.
examples.jsx:
<Nudge
  title="Split payment"
  body="Pay ₹12,000 in 3 monthly instalments."
  buttonLabel="See plans"
  onPressButton={() => {}}
  onClose={() => {}}
  modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Context: 'Nudge&Alert', AppearanceBrand: 'Secondary' }}
/>

from.quote: The screen handles its button and removes it on close.

examples.purpose: Inline compact, with no close button: one line of text with the button beside it.
examples.jsx:
<Nudge
  type="inline-compact"
  body="Set up autopay so you never miss a bill."
  buttonLabel="Set up"
  onPressButton={() => {}}
  showClose={false}
  modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Context: 'Nudge&Alert' }}
/>

examples.purpose: Stacked detailed: a title over list items, with no button or close.
examples.jsx:
<Nudge type="stacked-detailed" title="Why split this payment?" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Context: 'Nudge&Alert' }}>
  <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="No extra cost" supportText="You pay ₹12,000 in total" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Context: 'Nudge&Alert' }} />
  <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Three monthly payments" supportText="₹4,000 on the 5th of each month" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Context: 'Nudge&Alert' }} />
</Nudge>
